beer-hagolah/1:ב: Tur in the name of Rambam in chapter 3
beer-hagolah/3:ה: The gemara's emendation there and most of it is read entirely as Rambam explains in chapter 2, and likewise Tur and Orach Chayyim
beer-hagolah/14:ב: Tur in the name of Yerushalmi
beer-hagolah/16:_: Tur in the name of Yerushalmi in chapter 4 of Megillah
beer-hagolah/17:ב: Such are the words of Rambam; but Tur wrote: he spreads and reads, as one view wrote siman 57 — and spreads it like a letter even what he will read later
beur-hagra/5:ב: However. As written in seif 13 and he should not interrupt etc. that it is forbidden etc., all the more in such a case:
beur-hagra/17:ג: (3) He returns and rolls it, etc. — not like Magen Avraham in name of Sedei Chemed; and see in Kessef Mishneh there is no substance in his words; and so in Maharil: once the reader opened berachat HaEl HaGadol after reading before they rolled the Megillah scroll and Maharil rebuked him and they were silent until they rolled the Megillah to one roll and placed it before him; then he returned and began and blessed; and so the language "he returns and rolls and blesses" — end; and Baal Magen Avraham did not see Maharif's book, only what is written in such a case as known; and Sedei Chemed's distinction has no dawn:
beur-hagra/18:ד: (4) And if you read it in congregation, etc. — all of it in name of Raavad: we say in Yerushalmi on those who advance and only with ten; and should read: in its time not required; and reason: since all read as written here; see Yerushalmi chapter 1 halacha 5; and in end of chapter how we roast etc. Rava said and likewise for prayer, etc.; and Tosafot there; and it implies Shafi's view: if there is in such a case ten, the individual hearing outside if he can answer kadosh and kedusha — Ran in end of chapter 3 of Rosh Hashanah: how establish Rav on the Mishnah there; and likewise one who passed behind synagogue and heard, etc.; and we say in first chapter of Megillah Rav felt for R' Elazar as above and required ten even in its time; see there Ran who urged on this; but per this it is fine; but all this is per those who say what is written regarding ten is for delay; but R' Akiva argues on this as above:
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Mechaber seif 17 in Hagahah: and one should not annul. NB see responsa Chasam Sofer Orach Chayyim siman 91 and Chasam Sofer Yoreh Deah siman 191; and it appears to me the reason to make noise and confuse the ears of listeners so they will not hear this name of the haggadic pointing gesture:
chatam-sofer/3:_: (there in Magen Avraham) in majority of Israel they can annul — see there; NB that they brought at end s.v. but etc. — a matter they did not fix from the outset except for one place and spread there; for them it was as spread in majority of Israel — see there:
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (there seif 13) There was one who wrote while reading a verse in Megillah that he copies from it and writes it if he set his heart to fulfill yotzei, etc. NB it appears in my humble opinion a new law and it is correct, may it be so: even if he set his heart it helps only for an individual in this if he set his heart to fulfill; but in congregation this does not help. And it is similar to what Talmud and Shulchan Aruch wrote below siman 691: one does not read in congregation Megillah written between the lines; if he read he does not fulfill yotzei unless there is recognition it is long or short. If so proven in congregation intent of heart to fulfill does not help — only that it be evident he reads for Megillah; and if so here too if he writes, expounds, proofreads — in act it is not evident if he reads for mitzvah or to write and expound and proofread — therefore not better than Megillah written between lines that is not evident — perforce the reason: since not evident they do not know if it is Megillah — likewise if not evident if he read for mitzvah it does not help in congregation; see Magen Avraham siman 691 who wrote every ten is called congregation — see there. And with this we placed on correct everyone's words in Kol Bo who brought Korban Eidah in Yerushalmi chapter 2 halacha 2 regarding "there was one who wrote it" — you said Purim is permitted in doing melacha and answered: said on the fourteenth in walled cities — end Yerushalmi; and Korban Eidah in Shirrei Korban brought everyone's words in Kol Bo who brought Yerushalmi's difficulty and answers everyone in Kol Bo that it was time of pressure; Korban Eidah wondered why he was not satisfied with Yerushalmi's answer that it deals with the 14th in walled cities and left in requires study; and per my words it will come out well: behold the above law appears clear to examiner in Rashi and Ran and Beit Yosef who brought them: reason invalid between lines is because not evident if like reading Scripture — no publicizing miracle; and if so here too if he wrote, expounded, proofread — not evident it is for mitzvah — no publicizing miracle; and per this it comes out well: since we hold Megillah in its time for individual, not in its time with ten; and proven in Talmud daf 5 that even in walled cities on erev also considered not in its time and is with ten; and if so difficult how say he wrote on the 14th in walled cities — behold then we require ten and then intent does not help. But Yerushalmi per its method: examiner in Yerushalmi first chapter Megillah halacha 3: R' Avina in name of R' Asi: all they said postpone to day of entry, and specifically with ten — if so proven whoever is not postponed to day of entry even though postponed to erev — nevertheless does not require ten; therefore answers well Mishnah deals with the 14th in walled cities; but Kol Bo follows our Talmud's method who holds even in walled cities on the 14th ten required — impossible to explain it deals with the 14th since ten is called congregation — therefore must explain another matter; examine: even if others already fulfilled yotzei — nevertheless since we require ten and require publicity — "there was one who wrote" does not help; examine. And do not challenge on our words: if so for R' Asi who holds whether in its time or not in its time with ten — how explain Mishnah "there was one who wrote," etc.; this is not — R' Asi holds Megillah written between lines also fulfills in congregation and argues on R' Yochanan; for without this he argues on R' Yochanan: R' Yochanan holds permitted even for individual and he holds congregation required as Tosafot s.v. if so — also here he argues on R' Yochanan; and on the contrary here it will come out well: this depends on that — R' Yochanan per his method holds in congregation not fulfilled written between lines — perforce from Mishnah "there was one who wrote" fulfills even individual as said; but R' Asi holds fulfills in congregation written between lines — therefore no proof from Mishnah he wrote fulfills individual — therefore holds congregation required. And for us who hold like R' Yochanan not fulfilled written between lines and hold not in its time even on the 14th ten required — impossible to answer like Yerushalmi; and our words in Kol Bo come out well, may it be so, on correct; examine on this:
kaf-hachayyim/12:_: 12) There. One must read it entirely. The matter is clear reading inhibits even one section — if they did not read, he did not fulfill. Mateh Yehonatan. And in responsum Rashba siman 467 explained: even if one word missing — reader or listener — if he did not hear even one word he did not fulfill — see there. And so Magen Avraham s.k. 15. Avodat Yisrael letter 76. And see further below letter 16 and letter 82:
kaf-hachayyim/16:_: 16) There. If the scribe omitted, etc. — and it appears to me not required to read them orally except letters that ruin reading such as "and these days of Purim shall not pass" — if he omitted the word "not" he did not ruin reading; likewise mem of "and gifts for the poor" and similar; but if he omitted other letters or other words that do not ruin reading — he fulfilled even though he did not read them at all. Riaz, Beit Yosef in Hagahot, Magen Avraham s.k. 4. Except Magen Avraham wrote there on Riaz's above words: for below seif 14 it does not imply so. And so Pri Chadash below seif 14: all who lack anything in reading even one word — did not fulfill; and wrote on Riaz's above words: not clarified — see there. And so above letter 12:
kol-yaakov/1:_: (1) Seif 1: one should not be concerned in which script it is written. And such is Maran's view as demonstrated in Beit Yosef; and so Yoreh Deah siman 688; but Maran took Rambam's language as his way, for such are Rambam's words Laws of Megillah chapter 2 halacha 4; and such is Rashba's view — they brought from Avodat Yisrael letter 6; and such is Radbaz's view in Rambam's language siman 126; but per Riaz they brought Tosafot chapter 2 of Megillah and Tashbetz in his responsa part 1 siman 8; and Tosafot and Pri Chadash letter 9 — it seems to them: even though they validated other languages in Megillah, writing must be Assyrian which is holy tongue script, not other scripts. And for law it appears primary like Maran and his colleagues that it is valid; and so Rav Chakal ch. 1 siman 234 Orach Chayyim letter 9, Biur Halacha letter 16; but l'chatchila one should heed Riaz, Tashbetz, Tosafot, Pri Chadash not to fulfill yotzei except in Megillah writing Assyrian script and Assyrian language; and so Chakal there in Biur Halacha there [and Biur HaGra letter 20 on Hagahah words that it is an error is wondrous, for great poskim hold thus Rashbam, Rashba, Maran, Radbaz; and what he challenged from Mishnah until written Assyrian, etc. — see what Tosafot answered and Shakhnehag Hagahot letter 1 siman 691 Shulchan Gavoah letter 15 from Avodat Yisrael there Orach Chayyim there Chakal there:]
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) between sitting, etc. and Essi' 106. The listener too must be at time of blessing; and there likewise regarding berachat haTorah; and the reason is not only because it is a matter of sanctity as Magen Avraham wrote there. But here the listener too must bless — except the blesser discharges the whole congregation with his blessing, as Magen Avraham wrote above siman 484 and below siman 692 s.k. 2; and the listener is like answering and as if he blesses; therefore the listener must stand like the blesser from law:
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: (s.k. 5) Even a little — see in Kessef Mishneh, etc., for on daf 18b it states: our Rabbis taught: if the scribe omitted letters or words or verses and the reader read them by heart — he fulfilled. And he challenges from Mishnah: if there were blurred letters — if their writing is recognizable it is valid, if not invalid. And answers: not difficult — this in whole (and likewise majority which is like whole) invalid; and this in part valid. And Rashba challenged from this: R' Chelbo in name of R' Shimon ben Gamliel — R' Acha: even per view one need not read whole Megillah from beginning — sufficient if he begins from "There was a Jew," etc. — nevertheless it must be written whole before him; implies if missing until "There was a Jew" — invalid. And why — here in part missing you said valid? (And must read: if Rashba does not argue on early commentator that Rama brought: if whole matter missing — invalid even in part; and perforce they do not argue, for Shulchan Aruch brought Rashba's law and also early commentator's law — therefore must read: since we hold per view one need not read except from "There was a Jew" onward — what is missing until "There was a Jew" is not law of whole matter missing — clear.) And Rashba wrote: R' Chelbo deals l'chatchila; and so language "must," etc.; and baraita deals b'dieved — teaches yotzei — meaning perforce Talmud knew R' Chelbo deals also b'dieved; from challenge on what we taught (and it is seif 13 below) "he would expound or write it — if he set his heart he fulfilled" — this writing: if we say he wrote verse by verse and reads each verse he wrote — and R' Chelbo requires it written whole; and impossible R' Chelbo deals only l'chatchila — what does he challenge on Mishnah "there was one who wrote" that deals b'dieved — teaches yotzei; or Talmud knew R' Chelbo deals also b'dieved and again clear. And from this Rashba proved: at beginning (and automatically at end) even missing part — invalid. And in Kessef Mishneh wrote: one can say no distinction — part even at beginning valid and they fulfill b'dieved; and R' Chelbo deals l'chatchila:
magen-avraham/17:ה: (5) and do not annul, etc. Rama wrote in responsum siman 21 in name of Maharik root 144: if the custom is found in some posek one does not annul it even in time of pressure one does not change custom as we say in Bnei Bishan; and even if the custom has a side of prohibition one does not annul it as Maharik wrote; and even in custom of one place they say it uproots halacha; however if the matter changed from what it was in rishonim' time they may change custom per the time — end. And from Rosh in commentaries of Semag: what we say custom uproots halacha — even majority of views hold forbidden and Talmud supports them; and custom built on Piskei or external books — they say custom uproots halacha — for certainly thus our ancestors received mouth to mouth — end (see Maharik and Shach and book Beit Shmuel); and specifically custom founded on enactments as Mordechai wrote; but custom without proof from Torah is only like mistaken judgment (Magen Avraham ch. 14); and matter decreed by vote — even known for what reason and reason voided — requires another vote to permit (gemara first chapter of Beitzah); and Beit Din cannot annul fellow Beit Din's words unless greater in wisdom and number; and every matter that is because of concern and concern passed — no other vote required as written Yoreh Deah siman 116 and Tosafot Beitzah see there; and in Yevamot daf 79 they wrote: in monetary matters they can annul fellow Beit Din's words because Beit Din's hefker is hefker; and at first glance does not imply so in Gittin daf 36 regarding prosbol — see there; however one can say there it is matter of prohibition that therefore they refrain from lending; see there in Tosafot; and matter whose prohibition did not spread in majority of Israel they can annul — see there; and see siman 15 in Nachalat Shiva many laws of customs and book Beit Shmuel:
magen-avraham/18:ב: (ב) There is to be satisfied. Indeed in Hagahot Maimoniot he is satisfied regarding minors and women, and it is a dispute in Tur siman 689:
mishnah-berurah/8:ב: (כו) He fulfilled — for the Achashteranim sons of the Ramachim — even we do not know what they are; we require only the mitzvah of reading and publicizing the miracle; and even l'chatchila likewise; and therefore women and amei ha'aretz also fulfill. Peri Megadim wrote: every yirei shamayim should have a kosher Megillah in hand and read word by word in a whisper, for impossible to hear from the shaliach tzibbur because of the noise and confusion when they strike wood and make sound; fitting for all Israel who have ability [Peri Megadim]; and see below siman 690 seif 4.
mishnah-berurah/17:ב: (נו) And spreads it like a letter — meaning he spreads it all and does not leave it rolled, rather folds page on page; and beware not to drag it on the ground [Avodat Yisrael and Pri Chadash]; and see Peri Megadim who wrote: on the ground — likewise hanging above the table; and stand also is disgrace to holy scriptures. Further wrote spreading should be before he begins to bless so there is no interruption between blessing and reading:
peri-megadim/7:_: There is 17 — this is Ran's words and Avodat Yisrael in name of Ramban z"l. And Rivash's reason because of Achashteranim — we do not know foreign tongue — one can say to write that verse in holy tongue; see amud haemek letter 12: l'chatchila forbidden to read in two languages — likewise to be written in two languages is not correct; and see there will be explained; see amud haemek letter 6:
peri-megadim/9:_: From beginning 17 — ten sons of Haman were officers over those five hundred; and Rama wrote l'chatchila, etc. — it is like letter 11, for to Mechaber l'chatchila suffices only ten sons of Haman in one breath:
peri-megadim/10:א: (1) Reads 17 — because Mechaber's language is R' Moshe z"l's language; and in Tur not so; see Be'er HaGolah letter Chet. Custom to spread it all before reading; and Avodat Yisrael letter 12: spread sheet over sheet and see impossible to spread entirely on table — not sheet over sheet — better as whole open letter. Further Avodat Yisrael in name of Shakh wrote beware not drag on ground; and so Pri Chadash; and see on ground — likewise hanging above table; and stand also disgrace holy scriptures as siman 691 regarding reader in book rolled on wall — see impossible spread before blessings lest rolling be interruption between blessing and reading; and in Torah scroll too spread and see and bless; but final blessing does not apply to shield; and see Magen Avraham letter Dalet I will explain further. Mechaber in seif 14: reader and listener must intend — mitzvot require intent; and nevertheless chapter 2 Megillah wrote possible here all agree; and Avodat Yisrael in TKPT on shofar: where act was done — one can say no intent required; and in reading intent required except Megillah chapter "the reader" challenges from Shema if he set his heart — on the face of it from this. And Magen Avraham siman 60 letter Gimel in name of Radbaz: d'rabbanan mitzvah — one can say no intent; and one can say Megillah d'oraisa like Torah law; see Rosh Hashanah 28 and Pri Chadash here. And Magen Avraham there letter Dalet: whole section requires intent — mitzvot require intent; and Magen Avraham siman 63 letter Chet: one verse of Torah and rest d'rabbanan — if so plainly rest d'rabbanan if did not intend at all he fulfilled since d'rabbanan; however all who intended another matter or not to fulfill — plainly even d'rabbanan he did not fulfill like one who opened in wine and concluded in beer and that of matzah — benefited; and Avodat Yisrael 75 and TKPT; and above laws of Shema and other places I extended:
turei-zahav/17:_: He reads and spreads like a letter. It implies he does not spread only what he reads; but Tur wrote the reverse: he spreads and reads like a letter — implies he spreads first before reading, and so is the custom:
yad-ephraim/4:_: s.k. 15 was written in error and should read: below on "and the listener must" etc.:
yad-ephraim/7:_: In Hagahah seif 18: and when individual reads, etc. — see Beit Yosef who appears early commentator in name of Raavad: even b'dieved individual should not read whenever there are not ten; and if so Rama who wrote afterward when individual reads must bless implies even without congregation; and from that he did not write to disagree with Shulchan Aruch — appears he ruled like Raavad l'chatchila; requires study from where it appears Raavad likewise to reject Tosafot and other poskim' proof from R' Yochanan: in congregation it is different; and also answered thus Ran's and poskim's difficulties from one who passed behind synagogue, etc.; and explained other poskim argue on Raavad and do not divide thus; and if so per them l'chatchila ten required even without congregation:
